# KB Schema — the contract for ~/kb

A knowledge base for AI agents and humans, accumulated across vibe-coding sessions.
**Design goal: any session can find the exact note it needs in ≤2 file reads
(index → note), or one `kb search` call.** Read this file before writing to the KB.

Full rationale and research backing: `notes/kb-0001-kb-design.md`.

## Layout

```
~/kb/
  SCHEMA.md    # this file — conventions (human-owned control surface)
  index.md     # THE ROUTER. Generated by `kb reindex`. Never edit by hand.
  log.md       # append-only journal. Written by the CLI. `## [date] op | id | title`
  notes/       # atomic notes. flat. kebab-case. one idea each
  refs/        # large reference docs kept WHOLE (guides, manuals) + section maps
  raw/         # ingested sources + session-distill proposals. Append-only; only
               #   allowed edit is the `> ingested:/rejected:` promotion marker
  bin/kb       # the CLI — PEP 723 script, runs via uv-managed Python 3.12 (kb-0012)
  .kb.db       # sqlite FTS5 index. derived. regenerate with `kb reindex`
  .kb-embed.json  # note embeddings (aibox text-embedding-v4). derived. `kb embed`
```

## The two unit types

1. **Atomic note** (`notes/`): one idea, ≤400 words (lint warns at 450, errors at 600).
   Claim-style filename (`grubby-syncs-etc-kernel-cmdline.md`, not `grub-stuff.md`).
   The load-bearing fact goes in the FIRST sentence (models attend to tops of docs).
   Self-contained: readable with zero other context. No "as discussed above".
2. **Reference doc** (`refs/`): large docs that lose value if chunked (guides, manuals).
   Kept whole. Each gets a companion atomic note of type `reference` containing a
   **section map** (`## N. Title — one line`) so agents grep the map, then read the
   exact section with an offset — never the whole file.

## Note frontmatter (every note)

```yaml
---
id: kb-0042                      # stable anchor. assigned by `kb new`. grep for it
title: "Claim-style title: the fact, not the topic"
type: gotcha                     # fact|gotcha|howto|decision|reference|project|session
domain: fedora                   # lowercase. index.md groups by this
tags: [grub, kernel]             # lowercase kebab. topical
aliases: [boot args, kernel cmdline]  # synonyms — powers FTS + vocabulary mismatch
triggers:                        # WHEN an agent should read this. third person
  - "editing kernel cmdline or boot args on fedora-server"
status: verified                 # draft|active|verified|superseded
confidence: high                 # high|medium|low
created: 2026-08-02              # ISO dates only. never change created
updated: 2026-08-02              # bump on every edit (kb CLI does this)
verified: 2026-08-05             # stamped by `kb verify` (which flips status to verified); absent until first re-verification
supersedes: []                   # ids this note replaces (invalidate, don't delete)
related: [kb-0002]               # ids. 2-3 with a reason each, in the body link block
source: "url | memory:path | session"  # provenance. where the fact came from
summary: "≤200 chars. This line BECOMES the index.md entry. Make it route."
---
```

Rules:
- `summary` is the most important field — it is what future sessions see in index.md.
  Write it as a routing hint: what question does this note answer?
- `triggers` are matched against the current task. "Use when …" phrasing.
- Controlled vocabularies: stick to the enums above. `kb lint` rejects others.
- Dates: absolute ISO (`2026-08-02`), never "last week".

## Query protocol (read this when you NEED knowledge)

1. `cat ~/kb/index.md` — the whole file is small; read it. Pick the 1-2 entries whose
   summary/triggers match. Open exactly those notes.
2. If the index doesn't answer it: `kb search "sharp keywords"` (BM25-ranked, snippets).
   Use the sharpest token you have: error strings, ids, tool names beat vague nouns.
   Matching is AND-first: hits mean ALL terms are present; a "(partial match — …)"
   label tells you when it degraded to OR (treat those hits skeptically).
   A BM25 miss automatically retries as semantic vector search, gated at cosine ≥0.40
   and labeled — below ~0.45 is likely-absent territory, don't force-fit a hit.
   (Vectors kept fresh by a weekly cron `kb embed`; explicit semantic lookup:
   `kb vsearch "…"`.)
3. If still nothing: try one synonym (`aliases` exist for this), then conclude absent.
   **Budget: ≤5 search iterations total.** Over-searching is a documented failure mode.
4. Never bulk-read a folder. Every extra doc loaded is a measured distractor.
5. Cite by id (`kb-0042`) when answering, so claims stay traceable.

## Write protocol (read this when you LEARN something)

Save it when: a correction was made, a non-obvious fact was discovered, a decision was
made, a fix required real investigation. Do NOT save: anything derivable from reading
the code, ephemeral debugging, restatements of docs.

1. **GATE — search before creating**: `kb search "<topic>"`. If a note exists,
   UPDATE it (edit + `kb touch <id>`). New note only if genuinely new knowledge.
   (One contradicting stale note hurts more than ten missing ones.)
2. Create: `kb new --type gotcha --domain fedora --title "…"` → fill template in $EDITOR.
3. The CLI updates the FTS index and appends log.md automatically.
4. Run `kb reindex` after manual edits to regenerate index.md + FTS + git commit.
   `kb embed` (incremental, cheap) keeps semantic rescue current — it also runs weekly
   via cron (kb-0014), so manual runs are only needed after bulk note changes.
5. **Supersede, don't silently overwrite**: if a fact changed, run
   `kb supersede OLD --with NEW` — it links `supersedes:` on the new note, retires
   the old one (status: superseded + banner, excluded from search), and commits once.
   Old value stays discoverable.
6. Git is the undo button: the CLI auto-commits. Bad extraction → `git log`, revert.

## Ingest protocol (large external docs)

1. Drop original into `raw/` (immutable) or `refs/` (if it should stay browsable whole).
2. Create a `type: reference` note with a **section map** of the doc.
3. One source may touch several notes — extract atomic facts as their own notes and
   link back (`source:` field). The reference note stays the map; facts live atomic.

## Distill pipeline (automatic session capture → promotion)

A SessionEnd hook spawns a detached worker that reads the session transcript with a
cheap model and appends `## PROPOSAL` blocks to `raw/session-distill-DATE.md`.
The worker reads `index.md` first (write gate): it must not re-propose what a listed
note already covers; a proposal that *revises* an existing note carries
`- updates: kb-XXXX`.

- Proposals are CANDIDATES, not knowledge — they enter neither index.md nor FTS until
  promoted. Duplicate proposals across sessions mean knowledge is missing: promote.
- Promotion: review `raw/session-distill-*.md`; for each good proposal either `kb new`
  (with `source: raw/session-distill-…`) or apply the `updates:` target. Mark processed
  blocks with a trailing `> ingested: kb-XXXX` / `> rejected: <reason>` line — raw/
  stays append-only, but its review state stays visible.

## Session notes (continuity across sessions)

A `type: session` note is a dated log of one session — context for future
sessions, NOT knowledge. It lets a new session retrieve "what were we doing /
where did we stop" with one command, no keywords, no MEMORY.md dependency.

- Save on request ("save this session"): `kb new --type session --domain
  sessions --title "<date> <one-line topic>" --source session`. The `project:`
  field is stamped automatically (nearest git repo name; `machine` for ~).
- Body template: `## Summary` (2-4 sentences) / `## What changed` (files,
  configs) / `## Decisions` (+why) / `## Open threads` (next steps) /
  `## Pointers` (kb notes, handoffs, repos). Same 400-word budget as any note.
- Retrieve: `kb recent --here` first (current project only — multi-project
  volume can't drown it), plain `kb recent` as fallback, then `kb show <id>`.
- Session notes are excluded from index.md (routing surface stays topical) and
  from the distill pipeline, but stay in FTS ("what did we do about X" works).
- Durable knowledge learned during the session still goes through the LEARN
  protocol (separate fact/gotcha/… note) — the session note just points at it.

## Lint (run `kb lint` periodically, or after bulk edits)

Machine-checked: missing/invalid fields, bad enums, bad dates, `updated` before
`created`, dead `related`/`supersedes` ids, body `[[kb-…]]` links missing from
`related:`, empty `source:`, files missing from index, orphan index entries,
oversized notes, duplicate ids. NOT machine-checked (ask a fresh agent session, different model if
possible): contradictions between notes, staleness vs `source:`, claims that need
re-verification. Self-lint by the same model that wrote the notes has shared blind
spots — that's why structural checks live in the CLI.

## Maintenance (run periodically)

- `kb stale [--days N]` — ranks live notes by staleness (default 90d); flags
  STALE (updated ≥ N days ago) and NEVER-VERIFIED (≥ N/2 days old with no
  `verified:` date). Act with `kb verify`, an update, or supersede.
- `kb churn [--days N]` — ranks notes by git commit count in the window
  (default 90d; flag at ≥5 commits). A HIGH-CHURN note is a candidate for
  splitting, or for moving its stable core into `refs/` with a section map.

## Anti-patterns (each one is a documented failure mode)

- Index edited by hand → drift. It's generated. Curate `summary:` instead.
- "Just in case" notes / saving transcripts → hoarding: "remembered everything,
  discriminated nothing." Write gate exists for this.
- Verbosity creep → entries grow 4-8× in two weeks without a pruning force.
  The 400-word budget IS the pruning force. If it doesn't fit, split or cut.
- Copying mutable facts (versions, paths) into many notes → store once, link.
- Prose-only agreements ("we decided to…") → if it's not a note, it doesn't survive
  compaction. File it.
